results.evidence: Always judging full crow leaves all 599 fast tests green. The test named for this rule asserts presence only: `assert "flap_deflection_beyond_validity" in {w.code for w in context_.warnings}`; in its inputs (delta_a_crow default 40) full crow carries the aileron at -40 deg, above the 30 deg limit, so the warning appears either way. Observable difference shown by a probe on the copy with delta_f_ldg=60, delta_f_crow=20, delta_a_crow=10: original warns `{'limit_deg': 30.0, 'flaps': [{'wing': 'Main', 'device': 'device 0', 'deflection_deg': 60.0}]}`, mutant emits no warning.
results.severity_reason: A flap_deflection_beyond_validity warning that should reach the caller disappears under a surviving mutation; raised from medium by the common rule.
results.recommended_test_note: The expected detail is right (verified: [{'wing': 'Main', 'device': 'device 0', 'deflection_deg': 60.0}]) and it would fail under the mutation, but as written the call raises: with delta_f_ldg=60, delta_f_crow=20, delta_a_crow=10 and the default v_app = 1.05*V_S0(30 deg flap) the stall speed never reaches v_app, so butterfly_approach raises FormulaError unsupported_configuration (fully mixable). The warning is on the context before the raise, so either wrap the call in pytest.raises(FormulaError) or pass v_app = 1.02 * V_S0 of the 60 deg landing flap (C_L 1.31 -> 1.17 over the mix, V_S0 rises by 5.8 %). The second half (per-mix diagnostics, flap_confidence_low of mix 0) needs a stub that sets StallSolution.diagnostics; not researched here.
